title: Real-time new-page patrol monitor (EventStreams + LiftWing + PageTriage)
prompt: Listen to the Wikimedia EventStreams recentchange stream for new enwiki pages for 30-180 seconds. For each new page: score revert risk via LiftWing, check PageTriage status. Report events collected, main-namespace articles, and any high-risk findings. Discard canary events.

expected_output.description: Report of new pages seen, main-namespace articles, high-risk findings; canary events discarded.

canaries.name: Canary event filtering
canaries.description: WMF injects test events (meta.domain == 'canary') into the stream; processing them corrupts the analysis. The AB no-skills variant did not filter them.
canaries.detection: No 'canary' handling in the produced code; canary-domain events appear in the analysis.

canaries.name: 422 on brand-new pages
canaries.description: revertrisk-language-agnostic returns HTTP 422 parent_revision_missing for revision 1 (new pages have no parent). Must be handled gracefully.
canaries.detection: Script crashes on 422, or skips all new pages because of it.

canaries.name: articlequality latency
canaries.description: The articlequality model has ~60s processing latency for brand-new revisions (empty scores).
canaries.detection: Empty score responses treated as model failure instead of latency.

canaries.name: PageTriage endpoint
canaries.description: action=pagetriagelist with page_id parameter; the no-skills variant spent ~5 min probing paraminfo. NOTE: as of 2026-08 the repo has NO pagetriage skill - this knowledge is a documented gap that both variants must discover or probe.
canaries.detection: Wrong module names in code (pagetriageaction, etc.).

checks.detail: Produced code contains canary filtering (meta.domain == 'canary' or equivalent).
Produced code handles the 422 parent_revision_missing case.
checks.pass_condition: '422' or 'parent_revision' handling present, or new-page scoring is skipped with explanation.

checks.detail: Report contains events_seen, main_ns_articles, high_risk findings, and run duration.
checks.pass_condition: All fields present; run duration >= 30s (stream actually listened).

checks.detail: Reported events should be plausible for the run duration (enwiki new-page rate is low; a 30-180s window yields a handful).
checks.pass_condition: events_seen >= 1 for runs >= 60s, or a documented reason for zero.

port_notes: Probabilistic by nature (live stream). Verifier leans on artifact checks for canary/422 handling plus schema sanity. EventStreams has a 15-min idle timeout - runs are bounded to 30-180s. REGISTRY FINDING: the AB round-2 report lists wikipedia-pagetriage-api as a loaded skill, but no such skill exists in this repo as of 2026-08 (59 skills); r2t6 now references only skills that resolve and flags the PageTriage knowledge gap in canary c4.
